acceptance_items: the three frozen Session writes (permission.reply, session.cancel and the dedicated Session body ingress) perform one durable CAS write instead of refusing UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION, and the result reports only the accepted revision and never a Session state
an undeclared agentId is refused typed FORBIDDEN before any write, so the record path is never guessed
session.create and session.open stay typed UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION, because both must return real engine data and a one-way record cannot carry a response

the record has exactly one CAS fence: a stale expectation is REVISION_CONFLICT with the bytes untouched, a failed rename is uncertain with a real fence, and a malformed record is a typed throw never silently repaired
the reader keeps its own consumed watermark in its own data directory and reports the honest behind refusal instead of skipping a write the window already dropped
the watch applies in revision order and stops at the first write it cannot apply, so order is preserved and no write is silently skipped
permission.reply reaches the engine as a JSON-RPC response to the engine's own pending callback and selects only an optionId the engine really offered
the Console body reaches the engine verbatim as session/prompt, and session.cancel makes the daemon's own prompt end with stopReason cancelled
gaps: the control daemon still reports sessions: [] and notifications: [], so the Console sees neither the Session it writes to nor a permission identity from the projection; that projection is L10 and is not delivered here
session.create and session.open stay typed UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION and are deliberately not delivered

source-tree evidence only: the black box starts from the source CLI entry (the worktree generated/runtime-lib), not from an installed artifact, and there is no restart, deployed-entrypoint, cross-device or multi-account receipt
the engine is a local OpenAI-compatible stub provider, not an upstream model, so this proves that the write really reaches and is accepted by an engine, not any model quality

findings.evidence: control-protocol/console-api.ts:424-426 carries readonly optionId?: string and the parser validates it at :506-510; ui/teams-console/src/client/controller.ts:499-500 and render.ts:410,:563 send it; runtime/control-process.ts built the record change without it and runtime/acp-serve.ts guessed the first option of the projected kind
findings.fix: optionId is carried as an optional field through the store type, validation, parseIntent, intent construction and control-process; the watch uses the named engine option and refuses INVALID_ACP_FRAME when the engine never offered it or when it contradicts the stated decision; the kind is only the fallback for a command that named none
findings.red_green: two same-kind options with the second one named; reverting the named branch fails with optionId allow-always-a instead of allow-always-b
findings.real_entrypoint: the black box now sends the engine's real optionId and asserts the durable record carries it verbatim (50 checks, PASS); this engine's optionIds equal the projected kinds, so that step cannot by itself tell a named option from a same-kind guess, and the spec is what proves the difference

findings.evidence: startAcpServe called void sessionWatch.reconcile() on a 500ms interval with no in-flight guard, so a slow pass could be overlapped by the next one; both read the same watermark and could apply the same session.message twice, and a throw escaped as an unhandled rejection
findings.fix: createSessionIntentWatch keeps an in-flight guard, and the whole pass is wrapped so a throw is recorded as a typed refusal instead of escaping the interval callback
findings.red_green: a host whose receive blocks on a gate; without the guard the second pass prompts the engine again, failing with host.received length 2 instead of 1. The first version of this case depended on microtask order and passed without the guard, so it was rewritten to wait explicitly

findings.id: F3 check-then-act CAS loses a Console write
findings.evidence: sessionWrite reads the record and then calls writeSessionIntentRecord(path, current.revision, ...), and the store's own CAS is also read-then-rename, so two concurrent commands can both read revision N and then both rename; the later rename wins, one intent is lost, and both commands report ok:true
findings.fix: this daemon is the record's single writer, so its own writes are serialized through a promise chain
findings.red_green: two concurrent session.cancel commands; without serialization the record revision is 1 instead of 2, so one command was lost while both reported ok:true
findings.residual: the same check-then-act shape still exists on the already-merged relations write path (config/relations-intent-store.ts); this unit only fixed its own record

findings.id: F9 record had no span check
findings.evidence: parseRecord did not check that the intent count matches the revision span, so a record such as {revision:10, oldestRevision:1, intents:[5]} was read as valid; pendingSessionIntents then advanced the reader's watermark to 10 and silently skipped revisions 6..10
findings.fix: parseRecord now requires intents.length === revision - oldestRevision + 1 and refuses INVALID_INPUT otherwise, so the malformed record is never overwritten either
findings.residual: a record that is deleted and recreated needs a generation id in the watermark to be told apart from a normal record; that is not fixed and is recorded as a retained obligation

findings_note: Both findings are pre-existing and are reproduced on the unmodified base d531d24. Neither is fixed in this unit, because neither is this unit's defect.

resolved_defects.id: A1 watermark re-apply duplicates a Session body
resolved_defects.found_by: independent review attempt (attack A1), verified and fixed by the unit owner
resolved_defects.defect: A failed watermark save (or a crash) re-applied the same session.message on the next poll, so the engine received a second session/prompt and the Console user saw a duplicated message. The old code comment claimed the apply path refuses an already-satisfied write, which is true only for permission.reply, because that callback is consumed.
fix: an in-process high-water mark appliedThrough; base = max(durableWatermark, appliedThrough ?? 0), so a write already applied in this process is never re-applied
the watermark now saves appliedThrough ?? base, so a partial pass is also durable and the durable watermark never lags a write that already reached the engine
a store fault on the watermark save now maps through configFault like the record-read fault, instead of being flattened to ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE, which wrongly blamed the engine
the apply() comment now says true means the write really reached the engine
resolved_defects.red_green: runtime/session-intent-watch.spec.ts 'never re-applies a write it already applied when the watermark cannot be saved' uses chflags uchg so the watermark reads as 0 but cannot be written. Reverting base to the durable watermark alone makes it fail with host.received length 2 instead of 1, and setting appliedThrough = base also makes it fail; restored, the file is byte-identical and the spec is 12/12.
resolved_defects.residual_boundary: After a crash or restart, writes after the last saved watermark are still applied at least once, so a session.message can still repeat inside that window. This is the at-least-once boundary of this record shape and exactly-once is not claimed.

retained_obligations.detail: config/session-intent-store.ts repeats the atomic temp+rename, watermark and discard helpers of the already-merged config/relations-intent-store.ts. Extracting one shared helper touches merged code, so it is recorded instead of done here. Project AGENTS says to reuse a shared function for common semantics; this stays an open obligation.

the reader's watermark carries only appliedRevision. If the record file is deleted and recreated, the new record starts at revision 1 while the watermark may be higher, so pendingSessionIntents reports nothing to apply and the new writes are skipped until the record grows past the watermark. A record generation id carried in the watermark would tell the two apart. Not fixed.
the same read-then-rename CAS shape F3 fixed here still exists on the merged relations write path.
the control daemon still returns sessions: [] and notifications: [], so the Console cannot see the Session it writes to or a permission identity from the projection. That is L10.
both stay typed UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION because each must return real engine data that a one-way record cannot carry.
no installed-copy, restart, deployed-entrypoint or cross-device receipt for this unit.
